question: What main physical property sets lipids apart from other biological molecules?

options.A: They are built from identical repeating sugar units
options.B: They dissolve easily in nonpolar solvents
options.C: They contain nitrogen as their main structural element
options.D: They remain strictly solid at room temperature

explanation: Lipids are grouped together mainly because they do not mix well with water but dissolve easily in nonpolar solvents. [learn more](BMP113_U5_T2#BMP113_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why does a pregnant woman's body shift toward fat breakdown during late pregnancy?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for dietary fat intake throughout the third trimester
options.B: To cause an immediate drop in overall maternal blood pressure levels
options.C: To provide a steady energy supply for the mother while sparing glucose for the fetus
options.D: To prevent the formation of essential steroid hormones in the placental tissues

explanation: Breaking down stored fats in late pregnancy gives the mother energy while keeping precious glucose and amino acids available for the growing baby. [learn more](BMP113_U5_T2#BMP113_U5_T2_h1)

question: Which chemical components make up a standard triglyceride molecule?

options.A: One glycerol molecule and three fatty acid chains
options.B: Two sugar rings joined by a peptide bond
options.C: One phosphate group and two nitrogen bases
options.D: Three glycerol molecules and one free amino acid

explanation: Triglycerides are simple fats made by attaching three fatty acid chains to a single glycerol backbone. [learn more](BMP113_U5_T2#BMP113_U5_T2_h2)

question: What makes phospholipids so good at forming cell membranes?

options.A: They dissolve completely in watery blood plasma
options.B: They possess both hydrophilic and hydrophobic regions
options.C: They contain only rigid ring structures without tails
options.D: They bind permanently to circulating glucose molecules

explanation: Phospholipids have a water-loving head and a water-fearing tail, allowing them to form stable double-layered cell membranes. [learn more](BMP113_U5_T2#BMP113_U5_T2_h2)

question: What structural feature separates a saturated fatty acid from an unsaturated fatty acid?

options.A: Saturated fatty acids lack a terminal carboxylic acid group
options.B: Saturated fatty acids dissolve completely in pure water
options.C: Saturated fatty acids possess multiple ring structures
options.D: Saturated fatty acids contain only single bonds between carbon atoms

explanation: Single carbon-carbon bonds allow saturated fatty acids to pack closely together, which usually makes them solid at room temperature. [learn more](BMP113_U5_T2#BMP113_U5_T2_h3)

question: A pregnant client asks why she needs essential fatty acids in her diet. What is the best way to explain this?

options.A: Her body cannot make them, and they are vital for fetal brain and eye development
options.B: They ensure her body stores zero fat throughout the pregnancy
options.C: They prevent gestational diabetes by lowering blood pressure instantly
options.D: They act as direct replacements for all necessary protein requirements

explanation: Essential fatty acids must come from food because the body cannot manufacture them. They play a major role in building the baby's brain and eyes. [learn more](BMP113_U5_T2#BMP113_U5_T2_h3)

question: What core chemical structure defines all steroid molecules?

options.B: A complex branched amino acid chain

explanation: Steroids are easily recognized by their unique backbone of four interconnected carbon rings. [learn more](BMP113_U5_T2#BMP113_U5_T2_h4)

question: Which crucial substance is manufactured directly using cholesterol as a starting material?

options.B: Dietary starch stored in liver tissue
options.C: Steroid hormones like progesterone and estrogen
options.D: Hemoglobin pigments found in red blood cells

explanation: The body uses cholesterol as the building block to create essential hormones such as progesterone and estrogen. [learn more](BMP113_U5_T2#BMP113_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is the main job of the myelin sheath around nerve cell fibers?

options.A: To anchor the brain firmly against the cranial bones
options.B: To supply direct glucose molecules to resting neurons
options.C: To manufacture steroid hormones within the central nervous system
options.D: To insulate nerve fibers and speed up electrical impulse transmission

explanation: Myelin is a lipid-rich layer that wraps around nerves to insulate them and help electrical signals travel much faster. [learn more](BMP113_U5_T2#BMP113_U5_T2_h5)

question: Why should a midwife pay attention to major lipid imbalances during pregnancy?

options.A: Abnormal lipid counts prevent the placenta from attaching to the uterine wall
options.B: High fat levels immediately stop all breast milk production after delivery
options.C: Unchecked dyslipidemia can increase the risk of conditions like pre-eclampsia and fetal macrosomia
options.D: Maternal fat storage stops all calcium absorption in the gut

explanation: Severe imbalances in blood fats during pregnancy can contribute to vascular issues like pre-eclampsia and lead to a larger baby, known as fetal macrosomia. [learn more](BMP113_U5_T2#BMP113_U5_T2_h5)
